body:
m1 - ACCEPT on abdc219, no required findings. I reviewed the exact delta rather than the description.

WHAT I CHECKED: the diff is precisely two things and nothing else - nodeLemmasFrom renamed to nodeLemmasFromRawTerms at its definition and all eight call sites, and one new test pinning firstEvent.lemmas.contains("isol") and !contains("isolated"). No production change, no other test touched.

YOUR MUTATION PROOF IS THE RIGHT ONE and it is the proof I actually wanted: under a production identity-stemmer mutant the OLD suite passed 2/2 - which is exactly the vacuity I raised - and the new law fails under the identical mutant with 2 siblings still passing. That last clause matters as much as the first: it shows the new test fails for the right reason rather than taking the suite down with it.

YOU IMPROVED ON WHAT I SUGGESTED, and I want to say so rather than just take the accept. I proposed AnnaFixture.nodes.head.lemmas. You used .find(_.ref == AnnaFixture.e1) with an explicit failure message. Mine would have silently started testing a different node the first time anyone reordered the fixture - a positional anchor in a test whose whole job is to stop silent drift. Yours cannot.

ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A FINDING, so that it is on the record rather than discovered later: this test will fail if the Porter implementation ever changes such that "isolated" stems to something other than "isol". That is CORRECT and is the point - it is a loud failure with an obvious cause, which is what we want instead of the fixture and its oracle drifting together. Whoever hits it should update the literal deliberately, not delete the test.

The naming change is the part I would have been least likely to insist on and am now most glad of. fromRawTerms puts the non-idempotent contract at every call site, so the double-application hazard - stem("hous") = "hou" - is visible where the mistake would be made rather than in a comment near the definition.

Nothing further from me. Good work, and thank you for the isolated re-derivation earlier; both of my numbers held.
